title: How do I grow organic traffic?
clarifying: Primary goal – traffic volume, leads/revenue, or brand visibility on AI search?
Any constraints on resources (writers, dev capacity, link-building budget)?
Specific market or geo focus, or workspace-wide?
synonyms: increase organic traffic / get more traffic from Google
organic growth plan / SEO strategy for growth
more leads from SEO / grow non-branded clicks
improve AI search presence (routes here when goal-level, to Q11 when tactical)
structure:
Router tree. S1 picks the primary goal (volume / leads-BOFU / brand-AI), each with its own
data pull. S2 checks the goal-metric trend; declining hands to Q4 first. S3 selects the
dominant growth lever across 8 branches (technical regression, cannibalization, refresh
upside, coverage gap, AI-search weakness, authority gap, competitor surge, all-clean),
seven of which hand off; the all-clean branch is a rich TERMINAL (compound + whitespace
exploration, re-enter in 90 days).
changes: [P1] S3 has 8 lever branches with no declared evaluation order. Multiple levers will fire simultaneously on most real workspaces. Add explicit priority: technical regression > cannibalization > refresh > coverage gap > AI weakness > authority > competitor surge, OR score each fired lever by impact/effort and pick top 2.

[P1] S3 all-clean terminal packs strategy, whitespace analysis, experiments and cadence into one node. Split into 3 terminals (compound plan / whitespace plays / stretch experiment) so runs are loggable and verifiable.
[P2] The three S1 data pulls repeat sources. Factor into one shared data-pull node with goal-specific extensions to cut API cost when the goal is ambiguous.
[P2] Declining-trend branch hands to Q4 unconditionally; add a fast-path when the cause is already known from the data pull (e.g. index coverage collapse → Q12 directly).
[P3] Add resource-constraint input (from clarifying Q2) as a filter on S3 lever selection — currently collected but unused.

structure:
Linear pipeline with two decisions. S1 cadence selects the data window (7d / 30d+YoY /
90d+YoY), then a shared spine: compute 5-state verdict → dominant story + top wins/losses →
risk surface + crisis_flag → next-period plan. S2 audience forks into three format tracks

changes: [P1] crisis_flag=true formats a crisis section but never investigates. Add HANDOFF to Q4 (and Q26 for availability incidents) when crisis_flag fires and cause is unknown — report should link the diagnosis run.
[P1] "Compute 5-state verdict" is undefined in the tree. Document the 5 states and their thresholds in the parameter table (e.g. surging / healthy / flat / eroding / crisis).
[P2] Weekly cadence lacks YoY; add WoW + 4-week rolling baseline so the verdict logic is cadence-consistent.
[P2] "Save CMS" terminals need a verification signal (URL of saved report + distribution step: email/Slack).
[P3] Add optional Atlas/GEO KPI block to CMO and leadership tracks — currently only the team track carries Atlas tactical detail.

title: Why did my organic traffic drop?
clarifying: How big is the drop in percent?
When did it start – sudden or gradual?
Site-wide, a specific cluster, or a single page?
Branded or non-branded?
synonyms: traffic dropped / clicks are down / lost rankings suddenly

did Google penalize us
structure:
The densest diagnostic. Confirms the drop is real (seasonality, tracking, branded split),
then walks cause categories through chained decisions: measurement/tracking artifact,
algorithm-update alignment (→Q7), manual action, technical regression (→Q9),
SERP-feature/AI-overview displacement (→Q11), competitor displacement (→Q3),
cannibalization onset (→Q6), content decay (→Q8), single-page cases (→Q5). Multiple
cross-links between decision stages; terminals for no-measurable-impact and monitoring.
changes: [P1] This tree is the #1 loop source (Q4→Q3→Q8→Q11...). Its handoffs must carry the diagnosis payload and set run flag diagnosed=true so downstream trees do not re-enter Q4.
[P1] Seasonality check needs a defined baseline (YoY same-week ± STL decomposition) in the parameter table — "not seasonal" is currently judgment.

[P1] Add ordered evaluation: tracking artifact → manual action → algorithm update → technical → SERP/AI displacement → competitive → content. Cheap/definitive checks first; graph currently permits inconsistent entry order.
[P2] Add missing branch: index coverage collapse (mass deindexation) → HANDOFF Q12 (new). Today it is folded into "technical" and under-specified.
[P2] Add branch for AI-traffic substitution (impressions stable, clicks down, AI Overview present) with Atlas evidence → Q11; distinct from classic SERP-feature loss.
[P3] Cross-links make the visual unmaintainable; regenerate from structured source with stage layering.

content-keyword match and intent fit → on-page quality → striking distance check →
internal links → authority vs SERP → cannibalization → SERP feature dominance. Each stage

changes: [P1] Chain is ~9 stages deep; add early exits — if page is not indexed, hand to Q12 (new) immediately rather than continuing the on-page stages.
[P1] "Page been live" clarifying answer is unused: add an age gate (<8 weeks → set expectations terminal + indexing checks only).
[P2] Intent-fit stage needs a decidable test (SERP result-type mix vs page type) — currently subjective.
[P2] Authority stage threshold (page-level links vs top-10 median) to parameter table.

structure:
S1 verifies the update actually affected the site (window alignment + >10% magnitude);
mismatches route to Q4 or a monitor terminal. S2 classifies update type: spam update
(S3-spam: toxic backlinks → Q10 disavow path; on-page spam tactics → rewrite terminals),
reviews update (S3-reviews: add first-hand evidence, reviewer credentials → republish
terminals), core/HCU/unnamed (S3-quality: thin URLs, E-E-A-T gaps, duplication →

changes: [P1] Needs an update-catalog data source (confirmed updates + dates + type) so S1/S2 are decidable automatically; today classification relies on the user knowing the update.
[P2] Core-update branch terminal "wait and re-evaluate" needs a defined window (next confirmed update or 90d) and an interim action list.
[P2] Spam on-page branch overlaps Q9 territory (doorway detection); hand technical spam signals to Q9 instead of duplicating.
[P3] Add post-recovery measurement terminal: compare vs pre-update baseline, log recovery %.

S1 checks Atlas workspace + prompt setup (missing → create prompt set: commercial +
comparison + 3-6 early + competitors → baseline terminal). S2 classifies dominant
visibility gap: top-brand-visible-but-losing themes (S2a: chart losing themes → keyword

S4. Brand entity foundation — what's missing?

TERMINAL: Draft Wikipedia + submit AfC; else strengthen Wikidata + Google-indexes-both
Implement Organization schema + upgrade About + Person schema authors

title: Why aren't my pages being indexed?
clarifying: Single URL, a URL pattern/section, or site-wide?

Recent launch, migration, or CMS change?

crawled not indexed / URL not on Google / deindexed pages
rationale:
The most common technical complaint. Routes strictly on GSC's own exclusion reason,
because that is authoritative and machine-readable — every branch maps to one Index
Coverage state. Never-indexed vs deindexed changes urgency, not the branch logic.

S1. Scope?
Pull GSC URL Inspection: verdict, crawl date, canonical, referring sitemap/page
Pull GSC Index Coverage by exclusion reason + sitemap coverage + sample URL inspections
S2. Dominant GSC exclusion reason?
Discovered not crawled: check inlinks + sitemap presence + crawl stats for host load
S3. Why isn't Google crawling it?
HANDOFF: Q19 Orphan/deep pages — fix internal linking
HANDOFF: Q13 Crawl budget waste starving new URLs
Crawled not indexed: score content uniqueness, template thinness, near-dup ratio
S4. Quality signal?
HANDOFF: Q8 Improve/differentiate thin content
HANDOFF: Q18 Near-duplicate templates — consolidate

title: Where is my crawl budget going? (log-file & crawl-waste audit)
clarifying: Approximate indexable URL count (crawl budget matters mostly above ~100k)?
Server logs available (raw or via CDN), or GSC Crawl Stats only?
Triggered by slow discovery of new content, or general hygiene?
synonyms: crawl budget optimization / Googlebot wasting crawls / log file analysis
Google crawling wrong pages / slow to index new content
rationale:
Gate first: most sites do not have a crawl budget problem, and the honest terminal for
them prevents wasted effort. For large sites, waste categories are ranked by share of
Googlebot hits so the fix order is data-driven, not opinion.

nodes.label: Q13: Where is my crawl budget going?
S1. Is crawl budget actually a constraint?
TERMINAL: Not a constraint (<100k URLs, discovery lag <7d) — close; revisit only on scale change
Pull 30d logs (or GSC Crawl Stats): hits by status, path pattern, bot type, response time
Classify Googlebot hits: indexable / parameter / redirect / error / low-value pattern shares
S2. Dominant waste bucket (by % of hits)?

HANDOFF: Q17 Redirect chains consuming crawls

title: How do I fix Core Web Vitals and page speed?
clarifying: Which URL group(s) fail in GSC CWV report, or site-wide?
Field data (CrUX) failing, lab-only, or both?
Dev capacity available for template-level changes?
synonyms: core web vitals failing / LCP too slow / page speed fix
INP issues / CLS layout shift / PageSpeed score low
rationale:
Branches on the failing metric because remediation differs entirely per vital. Field
data governs (lab-only failures get a monitor terminal — Google uses field). TTFB is
pulled out separately since it is server-side and often masquerades as LCP.

nodes.label: Q14: How do I fix Core Web Vitals and page speed?
Pull GSC CWV by URL group + CrUX field data + PSI lab for representative URLs
S1. Field data failing?
TERMINAL: Lab-only failure — field passes; log, monitor monthly, no urgent action
S2. Which vital fails (worst URL-group first)?
TTFB >800ms: audit server/CDN — cache hit ratio, origin latency, DB queries
HANDOFF: Q26 Server/hosting/CDN remediation
LCP: identify LCP element per template; preload hero, optimize images (format/size/priority), remove render-blockers
S3. LCP element type?
Image LCP: AVIF/WebP + explicit dimensions + fetchpriority=high + CDN resize
Text LCP: inline critical CSS + font-display swap + preload fonts
INP: profile long tasks — break up JS, defer non-critical, remove heavy 3rd-party scripts
HANDOFF: Q15 Framework hydration dominates INP
CLS: reserve space (images/ads/embeds), avoid late-inject banners, stabilize fonts
TERMINAL: Deploy per template → verify PSI lab now, CrUX 28-day rolling green, GSC group passes

title: Is JavaScript rendering hurting my SEO?
clarifying: Framework (React/Next, Vue/Nuxt, Angular, other) and rendering mode (CSR/SSR/SSG)?
Symptom: content missing from index, links not discovered, or ranking underperformance?
synonyms: javascript SEO / Google can't see my content / CSR indexing problems
rendered HTML different / SPA not ranking
rationale:
Single decidable core test — diff raw HTML vs rendered DOM vs what GSC renders — then
branch on WHAT is missing (content, links, metadata) since each has a different fix and
different owner. AI crawlers mostly don't render JS, so a CSR finding also feeds Q25.

nodes.label: Q15: Is JavaScript rendering hurting my SEO?
Pull triple diff: raw HTML vs rendered DOM vs GSC-rendered HTML for template samples
S1. Does critical content differ between raw and rendered?
TERMINAL: Parity OK — JS not the issue; return findings to caller
S2. What is client-side only?
Body content client-only: enable SSR/SSG for template, or prerender at edge
Internal links client-only (onclick/router): output real <a href> in server HTML
HANDOFF: Q19 Re-audit link graph after fix
Title/meta/canonical/schema set by JS: move to server response; JS-set canonicals are unreliable
JS/CSS resources blocked by robots or 4xx: unblock, fix asset URLs
TERMINAL: Validate GSC live test renders fully; request recrawl
S3. Rendering fixed at source or needs infra?
Adopt SSR/SSG/ISR for SEO-critical routes
Interim: dynamic rendering/prerender service for bot user-agents (document as temporary)
HANDOFF: Q14 Hydration cost now dominates INP
TERMINAL: Verify GSC render parity + indexed text search ("site: + unique phrase") in 14d; notify Q25 (AI bots don't render JS)

title: How do I execute (or recover from) a site migration?
clarifying: Phase: planning, cutover imminent, or already migrated (and dropped)?
Migration type: domain, URL structure, replatform, redesign, or combination?
Full URL inventory + redirect map available?
synonyms: site migration SEO / domain change checklist / replatforming traffic loss
redesign killed traffic / URL structure change
rationale:
Phase is the master switch. Planning gets a gated checklist pipeline (benchmark →
mapping → staging validation → cutover plan). Post-migration drop gets a forensic
path ordered by kill-rate: redirects → directives → canonicals/internal links → parity.

nodes.label: Q16: How do I execute or recover from a site migration?
S1. Migration phase?
PLAN: Benchmark — export all URLs, rankings, traffic, links; freeze as baseline
PLAN: Build 1:1 redirect map (no mass-to-home); flag consolidations explicitly
PLAN: Staging crawl — validate redirects, canonicals, robots, sitemaps, parity on staging
S2. Staging validation clean?
Fix staging failures; re-crawl until clean
TERMINAL: Cutover runbook — deploy redirects at go-live, new sitemaps both GSC properties, monitor crawl stats daily 14d, keep old sitemap temporarily
POST: Pull pre/post crawl compare + GSC both properties + redirect coverage + log sample
S3. Dominant post-migration failure?
Missing/wrong redirects: generate gap list (old URLs → 404/wrong target) by traffic value
HANDOFF: Q17 Chains/loops introduced by migration
Staging directives left live: remove noindex/robots disallow from production
HANDOFF: Q22 Robots/sitemap cleanup
Canonicals/internal links point to old URLs: rewrite sitewide to final URLs
HANDOFF: Q14 Performance regression on new stack
HANDOFF: Q12 New URLs not entering index
HANDOFF: Q4 Drop not migration-correlated — general diagnosis
TERMINAL: Fixes deployed — track recovery vs baseline weekly; expected 4-12 week window; escalate if <80% at 12w

edges.cond: 1. Redirect coverage <95% of traffic-weighted old URLs
6. New URLs stuck out of index

title: How do I clean up redirects (chains, loops, wrong types)?
clarifying: Site-wide hygiene pass, or triggered by a migration/event?
Access to edit redirect rules (server config, CDN, CMS plugin)?
synonyms: redirect chains / redirect loops / 302 vs 301 audit
too many redirects / fix redirect hops
rationale:
One data pull (full crawl redirect map), then rank issue classes by equity and crawl
cost. Every terminal has a crawl-verifiable check, so this tree is fully automatable
end-to-end — a good first candidate for hands-off runs.

nodes.label: Q17: How do I clean up redirects?
Crawl full redirect map: source → hops → final status, type per hop, inlink count per source
S1. Dominant redirect issue (by traffic-weighted count)?
Chains ≥2 hops: collapse every source to final destination in one hop
Loops / redirect-to-4xx: map broken endpoints, decide final target or kill URL
Long-lived 302/307 on permanent moves: convert to 301/308
Protocol/host variants (http, www, case, trailing slash) not canonicalized in one hop: consolidate rules
Internal links pointing at redirecting URLs: rewrite links to final URLs (top pages first)
HANDOFF: Q16 Migration-scale redirect rebuild needed
HANDOFF: Q13 Verify crawl-waste reduction in logs after fix
TERMINAL: Re-crawl → 0 loops, chains <1%, all permanent moves 301/308; schedule quarterly re-crawl

title: How do I fix duplicate content and canonicalization?
clarifying: Technical duplicates (URL variants/templates) or editorial overlap (similar articles)?
Any syndication or multi-domain publishing involved?
synonyms: duplicate content fix / canonical tag issues / Google chose different canonical
same content multiple URLs / syndicated content SEO

nodes.label: Q18: How do I fix duplicate content and canonicalization?
S1. Duplication type?
HANDOFF: Q6 Editorial overlap — cannibalization tree
Pull duplicate clusters: crawl similarity ≥85%, GSC "duplicate" exclusions, canonical vs indexed-canonical diffs
S2. Dominant technical duplicate class?
Parameter/variant URLs duplicating canonicals
HANDOFF: Q24 Faceted/parameter strategy
Template near-dups (location/spec pages ≥85% same): add unique data blocks or consolidate + 301
Canonical conflicts: canonical ≠ Google-selected, canonical chains, canonical→noindex/redirect contradictions — fix to self-consistent rules
Syndication: enforce canonical-to-source (or noindex on partner), stagger publication, keep original richer
Cross-domain/staging dupes: canonical or noindex staging, consolidate microsites
TERMINAL: GSC duplicate exclusions -50% in 30d; Google-selected canonical = declared on sampled clusters
HANDOFF: Q12 If consolidation victims must re-enter index

edges.cond: 1. Different pages competing on same query (editorial)
Simple variants — canonical + one-hop redirect rules

title: How do I optimize internal linking and site architecture?
clarifying: Goal: fix defects (orphans/broken), boost specific priority pages, or restructure taxonomy?
List of priority URLs/clusters available?
synonyms: internal linking strategy / orphan pages / site structure SEO
link equity distribution / crawl depth too deep / topic clusters wiring
rationale:
Three distinct jobs sharing one link-graph pull: defect repair (objective, automatable),
equity steering toward priority pages (needs a priority list), and architecture
restructure (biggest, feeds pillar-cluster work in Q8/Q6). Goal drives the branch, not
symptom guessing.

nodes.label: Q19: How do I optimize internal linking and architecture?
Pull link graph: crawl (depth, inlinks, anchors) + GSC internal links + top-traffic and priority URLs
S1. Primary goal?
S2. Dominant defect?
Orphans: link each from its hub/category + related posts; add to sitemap
Depth >4 clicks: flatten via hub pages, pagination fixes, breadcrumb + nav paths
Broken/redirected internal links: fix targets to final 200 URLs, top pages first
TERMINAL: Re-crawl → 0 orphans on indexable set, depth ≤4 for 95%, broken internal links = 0
Priority pages under-linked: compare inlinks vs sibling median; add contextual links from high-equity relevant pages (traffic + DR donors)
Anchor audit: vary descriptive anchors, kill generic "click here", avoid one-anchor-everywhere
TERMINAL: Priority set inlinks ≥ sibling median; recheck rankings at 4w
S3. Restructure scope?
Design pillar-cluster map: pillar (broad) ↔ supporting (narrow) bidirectional wiring
HANDOFF: Q8 Missing pillar/supporting content to write
HANDOFF: Q6 Overlapping cluster pages to consolidate first
Nav/taxonomy revision: category consolidation, faceted nav rules, footer link hygiene
HANDOFF: Q13 Validate crawl distribution after restructure
TERMINAL: New architecture live — re-crawl, verify depth/equity distribution, monitor 8w

title: How do I handle international SEO and hreflang?
clarifying: Existing international setup, or planning expansion?
Structure: ccTLDs, subfolders, subdomains, or mixed?
Symptom: wrong country/language version ranking, or duplication between locales?
synonyms: hreflang errors / wrong country page ranking / international SEO setup
multilingual site SEO / geo-targeting
rationale:
Planning and debugging are opposite motions. Planning locks the structural decision
(subfolder default) before any tags. Debugging branches on hreflang validation output,
which is machine-checkable, plus the two failure modes tags can't fix (duplication
between same-language locales, weak local signals).

nodes.label: Q20: How do I handle international SEO and hreflang?
S1. Planning or debugging?
S2. PLAN: Structure choice constraints?
Default: subfolders on one domain (consolidated authority) + hreflang + GSC geo-targeting
ccTLDs only if legal/infra requires; accept split authority; plan per-country links
Implement hreflang: full return-tag matrix, x-default, self-reference, sitemap-based for scale
TERMINAL: Validate matrix with hreflang checker pre-launch; monitor International Targeting 30d
DEBUG: Pull hreflang validation + GSC per-locale performance + duplicate clusters across locales
S3. Dominant failure?
Missing return tags / invalid codes (en-UK→en-GB): regenerate matrix from locale registry
Canonical vs hreflang conflict (canonical crossing locales): self-canonical per locale, keep hreflang between them
HANDOFF: Q18 Same-language locales are near-dups (en-US vs en-GB) — differentiate or consolidate
Wrong version ranking despite valid tags: strengthen local signals — currency, address, local links, locale-specific content
HANDOFF: Q19 Locale sections orphaned from main architecture
TERMINAL: Validation errors = 0; right-version impression share per country rising over 60d

title: Is mobile parity hurting my rankings?
clarifying: Separate mobile experience (adaptive/dynamic serving) or responsive?
Symptom: GSC mobile usability flags, or suspicion of hidden mobile content?
synonyms: mobile SEO / mobile usability errors / mobile-first indexing issues
site broken on mobile / content hidden on mobile
rationale:
Google indexes mobile-only, so parity IS the index. Compact tree: parity diff first
(content/links/schema present on mobile?), then usability flags, then intrusive
interstitials. Speed issues route to Q14 rather than duplicating.

nodes.label: Q21: Is mobile parity hurting my rankings?
Pull mobile-vs-desktop diff (content, links, schema, meta) + GSC mobile usability + template samples
S1. Parity gap on mobile?
Content trimmed on mobile: restore full content (accordions fine — hidden-by-CSS is indexed; removed-from-DOM is not)
Nav/links reduced on mobile: expose crawlable menu links in mobile DOM
Schema/meta desktop-only: serve identical structured data on mobile
HANDOFF: Q15 Mobile DOM built client-side — rendering audit
S2. Usability flags?
Fix viewport, tap targets, font size, content wider than screen per GSC flagged templates
Intrusive interstitials/banners on entry: remove or reduce to compliant formats
HANDOFF: Q14 Mobile CWV failing
TERMINAL: Parity diff clean + GSC mobile usability 0 errors; re-inspect flagged templates in 14d

title: Are robots.txt, sitemaps, and directives configured correctly?
clarifying: Triggered by a specific incident (blocked pages, sitemap errors in GSC) or hygiene pass?
Who owns robots.txt / sitemap generation (CMS auto, dev, CDN)?
synonyms: robots.txt audit / sitemap errors / blocked by robots
noindex audit / crawl directives conflict / XML sitemap fix
rationale:
Directives are where single-line changes cause site-wide damage. Tree checks the three
layers in order of blast radius: robots.txt (crawl), meta/header directives (index),
sitemaps (discovery) — then conflict detection ACROSS layers, the class of bug audits
usually miss (e.g. noindex + blocked = noindex never seen).

nodes.label: Q22: Are robots, sitemaps, and directives configured correctly?
Pull robots.txt (+history), meta-robots/X-Robots-Tag crawl export, all sitemaps + GSC sitemap report
S1. Highest-blast-radius issue?
robots.txt blocks valuable paths (or blocks CSS/JS): rewrite rules; test each against sample URLs
Unintended noindex (template/CMS default, staging leftover): locate rule source, remove
Cross-layer conflicts: blocked+noindex (directive unseen), canonical→blocked URL, sitemap lists noindexed/redirected URLs — resolve to one consistent intent per URL
Sitemap defects: 404/redirect/noindex URLs listed, stale lastmod, >50k unsplit, missing sections — regenerate from canonical indexable set only
Bot-specific rules audit: verify Googlebot/Bingbot not throttled by CDN/WAF rules
HANDOFF: Q25 AI crawler access rules (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot)
TERMINAL: robots tester passes samples; GSC sitemap success, indexable set = sitemap set; add robots.txt change alerting
HANDOFF: Q12 Recover pages deindexed while blocked
HANDOFF: Q13 Directive changes shift crawl distribution — verify in logs

title: How do I implement structured data / schema at scale?
clarifying: Goal: rich results (SERP features), entity/brand strength (GEO), or fixing errors?
Which page types matter (product, article, FAQ, org, local, review)?
synonyms: schema markup / structured data errors / rich results not showing
JSON-LD implementation / FAQ schema / product schema
rationale:
Schema serves two masters now: Google rich results AND AI-engine entity grounding. Goal
splits the tree. Error-fixing is mechanical (GSC enhancement reports drive it); rollout
is template-driven; entity work hands finish to Q11 where its impact is measured.

nodes.label: Q23: How do I implement structured data at scale?
S1. Goal?
Pull GSC enhancement reports + Rich Results tests + Site Audit schema warnings
S2. Error class?
Invalid/missing required fields per type: fix template generators, not pages
Markup-content mismatch (schema claims not visible on page): align or remove — spam-policy risk
Deprecated types (FAQ/HowTo eligibility changes): keep for AI grounding, drop rich-result expectation
TERMINAL: Re-validate via Rich Results test; GSC errors → 0; watch feature impressions 28d
S3. ROLLOUT: Which page types first? (by traffic × feature eligibility)
Transactional: Product/Offer/Review + price/availability feeds parity
Editorial: Article + author Person + FAQ blocks where genuine questions exist
Foundation: Organization + WebSite + Breadcrumb sitewide, single @id graph
TERMINAL: Deploy per template → validate samples → monitor GSC enhancements + feature CTR
ENTITY: Build consistent entity graph — Organization @id referenced by all pages, sameAs to Wikidata/profiles, Person authors with credentials
HANDOFF: Q11 Measure entity impact on AI visibility
HANDOFF: Q26 Schema injection/hacked markup found

title: How do I control faceted navigation and parameter URLs?
clarifying: Rough count of parameter/facet URL combinations vs canonical pages?
Do any facet combinations have real search demand (e.g. "red running shoes")?
synonyms: faceted navigation SEO / filter URLs indexed / parameter handling
URL explosion from filters / crawl trap
rationale:
The one problem where BOTH over-blocking and under-blocking are expensive. Core move:
demand test per facet dimension — facets with search demand become indexable landing
pages (whitelist), everything else gets systematically excluded. Most trees treat facets
as pure waste; this one extracts the value first.

nodes.label: Q24: How do I control faceted navigation and parameter URLs?
Pull parameter inventory: crawl URL patterns + log hits per pattern + GSC indexed variants + keyword demand per facet dimension
S1. Is there index/crawl damage today?
Demand test per facet dimension: map facet values to query volume (e.g. brand, color+category)
S2. Facet dimensions with real demand?
Whitelist: make demand facets crawlable, indexable, self-canonical, unique title/H1/copy, in sitemap + internal links
HANDOFF: Q19 Wire whitelisted facet pages into architecture
Exclude the rest: canonical to parent + robots-block crawl-trap params (sort, view, session) + nofollow-free clean URLs in nav
S3. Already-indexed junk variants at scale?
Cleanup sequence: noindex first → wait for deindex → then robots-block (blocking first freezes noindex unseen)
TERMINAL: Indexed variants -80% in 60d; facet crawl share <10% of hits; whitelisted pages indexed
HANDOFF: Q13 Confirm crawl reallocation in logs
HANDOFF: Q18 Variant duplication beyond facets
HANDOFF: Q12 Whitelisted pages not entering index

edges.cond: 1. Yes — variants indexed or >20% crawl share

title: Can AI crawlers access and use my site? (technical GEO)
clarifying: Goal: be citable by AI engines, or also control/limit AI training use?
CDN/WAF in front of the site (Cloudflare, Akamai) and who controls its bot rules?
synonyms: GPTBot blocked / AI crawler access / llms.txt
ChatGPT can't read my site / Perplexity not crawling / bot blocking audit
rationale:
The technical half of GEO — Q11 assumes engines can read the site; this tree verifies it.
Key facts encoded: most AI crawlers execute no JS (CSR sites are invisible to them), CDN
bot-defense silently blocks them, and retrieval bots (ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot) matter
more for citations than training bots (GPTBot). Policy decision (allow vs block training)
is an explicit branch, not an assumption.

nodes.label: Q25: Can AI crawlers access and use my site?
Pull 30d logs filtered to AI UAs (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, Bytespider) + robots rules + CDN/WAF bot settings
S1. Are AI crawlers reaching the site?
Blocked in robots.txt: set per-bot policy — allow retrieval/search bots for citability; training bots per company policy
Blocked by CDN/WAF (403/challenge, zero hits despite no robots block): whitelist verified AI bot IP ranges / enable verified-bots category
S2. Bots arrive — can they READ the content?
HANDOFF: Q15 Content client-rendered — AI bots get empty shell
Content behind paywall/login/geo-wall: expose citable summary layer (lead paragraphs, key stats) or accept invisibility
Readability pass: answer-first sections, clean HTML hierarchy, dateModified, stable anchors; optional llms.txt index
S3. Access + readability OK — are retrieval bots actually fetching?
Low retrieval-bot hits: strengthen discovery — sitemaps fresh, key pages linked from crawled hubs, Bing indexation verified (Copilot + ChatGPT rely on Bing)
TERMINAL: AI bot hit share healthy on key pages; re-measure Atlas citation rate at 14/28d
HANDOFF: Q11 Access clean — visibility gap is content/entity side
HANDOFF: Q22 Robots rewrite alongside broader directive cleanup

edges.cond: 1. Retrieval-bot hits low on key pages

title: Is a server, security, or availability problem hurting SEO?
clarifying: Active incident (site down/hacked now) or intermittent/historical pattern?
Stack access: hosting, CDN, DNS, certificate management?
synonyms: 5xx errors SEO / site down Google impact / hacked site spam pages
SSL certificate error / mixed content / DNS issues crawling
rationale:
Ordered by urgency class: active compromise (hacked = existential, spam URLs + cloaking
must die fast) > availability (5xx patterns Google throttles on) > certificate/protocol >
mixed content. Hack branch includes the GSC security-issues + cleanup + review-request
sequence, then hands history-check to Q7 (spam-update interplay).

nodes.label: Q26: Is a server, security, or availability problem hurting SEO?
Pull GSC Security Issues + crawl stats (5xx trend) + uptime + cert status + logs (error spikes, odd URL creation)
S1. Issue class (worst first)?
COMPROMISE: quarantine — patch entry, remove injected pages/links/cloaking, rotate credentials
Serve 410 for spam URLs, purge caches/CDN, resubmit clean sitemap
GSC: request security review; document timeline
HANDOFF: Q7 If manual action / spam-update overlap on hacked period
5xx/availability: correlate error windows with crawl-rate drops; fix origin capacity, cache errors NEVER (no cached 5xx), tune CDN failover
HANDOFF: Q14 Chronic slowness beyond errors
DNS/certificate: fix expiry/chain/CAA; enforce single canonical host over 301; HSTS after validation
Mixed content / http leftovers: rewrite asset URLs, upgrade-insecure-requests, fix hardcoded http links
Overzealous WAF/rate limits throttling Googlebot: verify bot IPs, exempt verified crawlers
HANDOFF: Q22 Bot access rules audit
TERMINAL: 5xx <0.5% of crawls, cert valid, GSC security clean; add uptime + robots + cert alerting
HANDOFF: Q9 Full technical re-audit after incident closed

edges.cond: 1. Compromise: GSC security issue / injected spam URLs / cloaking
